messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate + p95 latency for Hosted API and Dedicated pools in aws us-west-1. Root cause suspected: spikes in AWS STS calls and upstream auth errors. PD runbook triggered.

maddie (oncall): I'm on it. Setting sev=2 for now. Observability shows STS throttling + gateway 504s. starting triage. @ryan can you grab net/rt metrics and token cache hit ratio?

ryan (sre): grabbing graphs. p50 ~ 800ms -> p95 ~ 3.2s for us-west-1 API frontends. STS AssumeRole error rate spiking ~ 40x baseline. token cache hitrate dropped from 98% -> 62% in the same window.

ow:
```
[2026-03-15T21:12:03Z] aws.sts.AssumeRole ThrottlingException Throttled
[2026-03-15T21:12:06Z] gateway upstream read timeout 504 service=hosting-api region=us-west-1
[2026-03-15T21:12:15Z] token_fetch failed status=502 provider=okta
```

ow jin: I'm seeing elevated egress latency to sts.amazonaws.com from the us-west-1 nodes, multiple AZs. AWS Health console shows "Service disruption in US West (N. California)??" (link pasted).

ow maddie (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle internal retries + increase exponential backoff 2) enable token-cache-fallback mode (serve cached tokens for 60s) 3) route a percentage of hosted traffic to us-east-1/dedicated pools in other regions 4) alert CS and post status page update.

ow owen: I'll push routing override. Rolling traffic weights: us-west-1 -> 60% -> 20% over 10m, us-east-1 take remainder. Command I ran:
```
# on control-plane
curl -X POST "$CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/routing/overrides" -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN" -d '{"region_weights": {"us-west-1":0.2,"us-east-1":0.8},"reason":"sts-egress-spike-us-west-1"}'
```

now maddie (oncall): applied temporary token-cache config: `TOKEN_CACHE_FALLBACK=60s` to hosted-proxy in us-west-1. This reduces auth traffic. Also increased gateway connection timeout to 30s.

now sarah (support): Customer impact: a subset of API requests to Hosted and Dedicated pools in us-west-1 are getting 5xx or long tail latency. I'm drafting a short notice for affected customers — will mention degraded performance in us-west-1 and mitigation steps.

now pagerduty: Pager duty note: Incident acknowledged by maddie. On-call handoff scheduled in 45m to owen (secondary).

now ryan (sre): After routing change and cache fallback we see service error rate drop from 12% -> 3.5% over last 8 minutes and p95 improved from 3.2s -> 1.1s. STS request rate reduced ~55% from token-cache. Still seeing occasional 502s for internal control-plane calls.

now maddie (oncall): chasing AWS support ticket for STS. Opening case ID: 1234567890, priority: high. Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/home#/case/?caseId=1234567890

now jin: Observability vendor (datadog) shows some ingestion lag for US west metrics ~1-2m delayed. pulling raw host metrics from internal graphite as backup.

now owen: I've started a canary rollback for one dedicated pool in us-west-1 to a smaller instance class to reduce egress pressure — scaling plan in k8s: `kubectl scale deployment rp-dedicated-usw1 --replicas=2` and adjusting pool-concurrency.

now maddie (oncall): customer comms: draft posted to #customer-facing-drafts for review. support will send targeted emails for top 15 accounts with traffic in us-west-1.

now status-bot: Status page updated: "Partial service degradation in US West (us-west-1) affecting Hosted API + Dedicated pools. Mitigations in progress. We'll provide updates every 30 minutes."

now owen: taking the active pager at 21:30 UTC. I'll own follow-ups and AWS ticket coordination. maddie, handing off timeline + actions in case notes.

maddie (oncall): handing off to @owen. Key actions completed: routing override applied, token-cache fallback enabled, gateway timeout increased, CS notified, AWS ticket opened. Next: monitor, await AWS update, consider cross-region failover for reserved Dedicated capacity if AWS doesn't recover.

now owen: ack. If we see errors rise >5% for 10m I'll escalate to execs and initiate broader dedicated pool failover. Current severity remains sev=2.

now incident-bot: Automated postmortem stub created: /incidents/2409876543-us-west-1-sts-egress-spike - responders: maddie, owen, ryan, jin, sarah. Please add timeline notes.

now maddie (oncall): adding quick notes: root cause suspected: AWS STS regional egress throttling combined with token cache TTL misconfig (short TTL led to cache misses and storm of STS calls). Long-term actions: 1) add jittered backoff + global token cache fallback, 2) add multi-region STS fanout + local retry budgets, 3) alerting for token-cache hitrate drops.

now sarah (support): CS emails sent to affected accounts at 21:28 UTC. Will update when responses come in.

now owen: I'll stay on until 22:30 UTC, then pass to next oncall (jin). If AWS confirms a regional issue, we'll plan a formal failover/maintenance window.

now ryan (sre): adding observability TODOs to the incident ticket: add histogram for STS latencies, token cache hitrate alert > drop of 10 percentage points, and an automatic routing guard if region error rate > 7% for 5m.

now maddie (oncall): marking this thread for follow-up retro. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
